name: CA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+6 district with a favorable national environment for Democrats
Incumbent Ami Bera has a large financial advantage ($1.8M cash vs $16K)
Markets price Bera at 95-96% to win
No public polling of the general election
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Bera: a D+6 seat, incumbency, a favorable environment, and a lopsided money edge over Robb Tucker, whose campaign has almost no cash on hand. Prediction markets on both Kalshi and Polymarket price his reelection around 95-96%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any late surge in Republican outside spending or a polling surprise showing Tucker within single digits would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ami Bera seeks another term in a Sacramento-area district that leans Democratic by about six points. He enters the general with roughly $1.8 million on hand after raising $1.25 million, while Republican Robb Tucker has raised about $258,000 and reports only $16,000 in cash. No outside groups are spending against either candidate, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive.

With no public general-election polling, the picture rests on fundamentals and markets, both of which favor Bera heavily. Kalshi and Polymarket each put his chances in the mid-90s. The main uncertainty is the absence of direct polling, which keeps uncertainty moderately wide, but every available signal points to a comfortable incumbent win.
